title: Tiered SLO dashboards + deploy/incident annotations (Hosted vs Dedicated views)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Adds tiered SLO dashboards (Hosted + Dedicated) with a comparison view, plus deploy/incident annotations for faster correlation during budget burn.
description: Summary: This PR adds a tiered SLO dashboard set to the observability-pack, including (1) Hosted SLO overview, (2) Dedicated SLO overview (tier-wide; no customer-level by default), and (3) a Dedicated vs Hosted comparison view. It also adds Grafana annotations for deploys and incidents so we can correlate latency spikes / streaming disconnects / 5xx bursts with changes and incident timelines. Motivation: Part of the Q1 reliability milestone to formalize tiered SLOs + error budgets, we need canonical, tier-aware views that match the new SLI tagging at ingress and avoid metric cardinality blowups. This PR is intended to be the “default” internal dashboard surface linked from burn-rate alerts and runbooks. Out of scope: customer-facing Dedicated per-account dashboards and access control (tracked in ENG-4946 follow-ups) and any changes to SLI definitions/recording rules (those land in the monorepo + telemetry repos). Dependencies/assumptions: Requires tier/deployment mode labels to be present on the primary request/latency/streaming metrics (see redwood PR-28411) and burn-rate recording rules to exist (redwood PR-28492). Key changes: (A) New dashboards: 1) SLO Overview — Hosted (tier=hosted, region filter, endpoint_class filter; panels for availability/success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming disconnect rate, and top contributors by endpoint_class + region). 2) SLO Overview — Dedicated (tier=dedicated; same core panels; includes headroom hints panel that links to fleet dashboards but does not embed per-customer dimensions). 3) SLO Compare — Hosted vs Dedicated (side-by-side availability, latency percentiles, and streaming reliability; uses a shared time range + shared region selection; intended for incident review and target negotiation with PM). (B) Annotation tracks: “Deploys” annotation fed by deploy event series (redwood_deploy_events_total + build SHA label, aggregated to avoid per-service noise), “Incidents” annotation fed by incident-bot exported events (incident_events_total) with severity and incident_id, and a “Budget burn state” annotation derived from burn-rate alert firing series for quick visual overlay. (C) Dashboard conventions: standard variables (region, endpoint_class, tier), consistent SLO links in panel descriptions, and a top-of-dashboard note on SLI exclusions (invalid requests, explicit rate limits, client aborts) to reduce confusion when support/PM teams compare dashboards with raw logs. (D) Cardinality guardrails: no per-model and no per-account breakdowns in the default dashboard; top contributors are capped to N=10 and use endpoint_class + route_group only (route_group is derived/normalized by recording rules). A hidden “__debug” toggle exists for SRE-only use to reveal model breakdown if the underlying metrics are safe; default is off. Validation: ran grafana-lint + jsonnet compilation; loaded dashboards into staging Grafana and verified variables resolve for us-east-1/eu-west-1; spot-checked that streaming disconnect panel does not include client aborts per current metric taxonomy. Screenshots: included in the PR conversation (staging links). Rollout: once merged, this pack is picked up by the weekly observability-pack sync job; SRE will pin alert runbook links to the new dashboard UIDs after deploy.
commits: dashboards/slo: add tiered SLO overview dashboards (hosted + dedicated)
grafana: add deploy + incident annotation queries and default styling
dashboards: standardize variables/templating and add SLO notes + runbook links
lint: add dashboard UID collision check in CI
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid any dependency on per-route raw labels? I’m worried about cardinality if folks start adding route=… panels ad hoc. Also, please add a short note in the dashboard about SLI exclusions (rate limited, invalid, client abort) so Support doesn’t misinterpret the gap vs access logs.

Sergio Costa (author): Good call. I switched all “top contributors” panels to use route_group (normalized) and added the SLI exclusions note + links to the SLI spec. Also added a hard cap topk(10) and set the default to endpoint_class only.

Thomas Baird (review): The deploy annotation query is grouping by service + sha; that can still get noisy in multi-service rollouts. Can we aggregate to a single event per environment and show sha in the annotation text instead?
Sergio Costa (author): Updated: deploy annotations now reduce to env+sha (and include service list as truncated text). Also added a 15m dedupe window so repeated deploy events don’t spam.

Aisha Bello (review): The streaming disconnect panel should explicitly exclude client aborts (we’ve had confusion on SUP-28501). Do we have a metric split we can rely on, or do we need to call that out as a known limitation?

Sergio Costa (author): The panel now uses stream_disconnects_total{reason!="client_abort"} and includes a tooltip note. If the reason label is missing, it will show as “unknown” and still count; that’s consistent with current SLI guidance. Added a link to the runbook section on classifying disconnects.

Felix Schneider (review): Comparison dashboard looks good, but can we align the time series colors across Hosted/Dedicated so screenshots don’t get confusing? Also add an explicit “Tier” legend label.
Sergio Costa (author): Done: hosted is always blue, dedicated always green, and legend labels are prefixed with the tier string.
Logan Wright (review): Please ensure the dashboards still render if burn-rate recording rules aren’t present (some regions lag during rollout).
Sergio Costa (author): Added “or vector(0)” fallback for burn panels and a banner panel that warns when the recording rule series is absent in the selected region/time range.
